selected_evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline healthy ping captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 254597f8... to 0023fc31...; post-restart IP/route/ping to node3 verified recovered.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, and eventual fully-automatic recovery (after fixing a persistence bug)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline BGP/route captured. First restart: boot_id changed (e5a08f0f->dd6abc4e) but BGP config was lost (bgpcfgd wipes manual vtysh edits) — diagnosed via bgpd.conf missing our neighbor line. After deploying+fixing a persistent systemd unit (fixing a dependency cycle), a clean third restart of node1 showed boot_id change (e66d0bbd->599cf113->dd6abc4e chain, final 599cf113) with the unit running automatically, BGP Established, route installed, and node3<->node4 ping succeeding with zero manual steps.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, fully-automatic recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured (561a6567...); reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 9d1740db...; [REDACTED].service ran automatically per journalctl; BGP session Established (PfxRcd=1) with route 192.168.13.0/24 installed; node4->node3 ping succeeded post-restart, confirming full automatic recovery.

selected_evidence.requirement: Final cross-cluster healthy-state confirmation after all 4 restarts
selected_evidence.summary: Final sweep: all 4 nodes report their post-restart boot_ids; BGP sessions Established on both switches with correct routes installed; node3 and node4 ping each other's private IPs successfully.
